Review the code in https://github.com/entireio/external-agents/pull/13.

Compare against https://github.com/entireio/roger-roger/pull/1/

Ensure CLI version is being preserved in transcript.jsonl
I’m pulling the PR diffs and the local codebase side by side so I can review PR #13 against `roger-roger` PR #1 and specifically trace whether `cli_version` survives into `transcript.jsonl`.

I’ve confirmed the local checkout is on `add-support-compact-transcripts`. Next I’m reading both PR diffs directly so the review is grounded in the exact code under discussion, not just the local branch state.

Both diffs are loaded now. I’m checking the surrounding protocol and transcript code in the repo to see whether PR #13 matches the `roger-roger` approach and whether version metadata is actually carried through the JSONL path instead of only reconstructed at export time.

I’ve narrowed the likely gap: PR #13 injects `cli_version` at compacting time from `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION`, but unlike the timestamp work in `roger-roger`, it doesn’t persist that value with the captured transcript itself. I’m checking the local transcript/session shapes and tests now so we can fix the preservation point rather than just re-derive it later.

I’ve confirmed there isn’t already a transcript-level preservation mechanism in this repo. I’m pulling the protocol doc next so the fix matches the actual compact-transcript contract rather than guessing from the tests alone.

content.text: The cleanest fix is looking like: store `cli_version` alongside the cached native transcript, teach parsing to carry that field through both CLI and IDE transcript shapes, and have compaction prefer the preserved value over the current environment. I’m patching that path now and adding tests that would fail if we ever regress back to “current env wins.”

I’m editing the preservation path now: the cached Kiro transcript will carry `cli_version`, compaction will prefer that stored value, and the tests are being updated so a future CLI upgrade can’t silently rewrite old session history.
The preservation change is in. I’m formatting and running the focused Kiro tests now to catch any mismatched assumptions in the existing transcript fixtures before I summarize review findings.
The repo is a multi-module layout, so the first test command missed the module root. I’m rerunning from `agents/entire-agent-kiro`, which is the actual Go module for this PR.

The code changes themselves are formatted. The test failure was just the Go build cache trying to write outside the sandbox, so I’m rerunning with `GOCACHE` pointed at `/tmp` to keep verification inside the workspace allowances.

content.text: I found two subtle issues in the test loop: the version-stamping helper was treating plain IDE transcripts as if they were already CLI-shaped, and one fallback test wasn’t setting `ENTIRE_CLI_VERSION` at all.
